purpose: Stage and independently review only inert content verification of already-pinned Local Mistral conversion identities.
requiredInvariants: This PR is inert and verifies bytes only for a caller-supplied already-pinned regular-file identity; it does not discover conversion roots, parse authority JSON, invoke Mistral, publish reviews/status, change verifier routing or activate a workflow.

The caller supplies the O_PATH identity FD plus the dev/inode identity captured by the admitted segment-8 primitive. This segment first revalidates that the supplied FD still refers to that exact regular-file identity.

Readable access is obtained only through the kernel-controlled /proc/self/fd/<integer-fd> handle and is accepted only when fstat proves the reopened descriptor has the exact same device and inode as the pinned identity.
A content source must be root-owned, have no owner/group/world write bits, and stay within the fixed per-artifact byte bound before any content authority is granted.
Mistral GGUF and llama-server require exact authority-provided byte sizes; conversion-report is bounded to 4 MiB and its exact content identity is the authority SHA-256.

The complete baseline device, inode, uid, mode, size, mtime_ns and ctime_ns tuple is revalidated immediately before and immediately after every read chunk, again before and after the EOF probe, and independently again after hashing.

The SHA-256 authority comparison is performed inside the same _hash_exact_fd routine before that routine can return success; any byte stream differing from the authority content fails closed even if a concurrent mutation were not otherwise visible through metadata.

Total bytes must equal the validated source size, early EOF and trailing bytes fail closed, and the accepted SHA-256 must exactly equal the supplied authority digest before content verification succeeds.
The returned readable FD is the same verified descriptor, rewound to offset zero; callers must consume that FD (or /proc/self/fd for that inherited FD) rather than reopen the original pathname.

Because the accepted source is root-owned and has no write permission bits, non-root reviewer/runtime processes cannot mutate the verified inode after acceptance; root is outside the untrusted review-input boundary.
All operating-system errors are translated to fixed ContentVerificationError codes with suppressed exception chaining; raw OS/path details are not emitted by this primitive.

Root discovery/authorization, authority-field binding, semantic validation, invocation, sensitive-output handling, attestation publication, provider status, exact-head routing and self-review prevention remain separately governed.
No product, API, database, RBAC, registration, cabinet, customer-data or production-routing behavior is activated.
Local Qwen is the independent reviewer because this changes future Local Mistral authority only.
REG.RU remains production authority and new recurring cost remains 0 RUB.
